title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Pool and spa servicing
audience: Solo operators and team owners of pool and spa servicing businesses who want repeat bookings and referrals from clients they have already served.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask at the moment the client is most satisfied
instruction.body: The best time to ask for a review or referral is after the client has confirmed the water result is right, usually when the test log has been shown and the visit is signed off. Ask in one sentence, name the next step you would like, such as a review or the name of one neighbour with a pool, and make it easy to decline. Record what you asked and what the client said. Timing matters: in one Baylor Keller Center experiment, a late reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one (1 June 2024). It was a single experiment. The AMA says timing should match the product, because experience goods need more evaluation time (10 January 2023). Google lets a business share a review link or QR code (Google Business Profile Help). Do not write reviews for clients or invent them. Asking only the happy clients is called review gating, and Podium, a vendor, says Google treats it as a violation (2 May 2022; not checked against Google's policy). Incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (ACCC, 15 July 2026). Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews, so check each platform's terms before offering any incentive.

instruction.heading: Offer the next service before the client leaves
instruction.body: Repeat work is the dependable core of a pool round. At sign-off, propose the next step with a date: a fortnightly service that continues, a pre-summer opening, a spring clean-up after the cover is removed, or a chemistry reset before a holiday rental season. Put the scope, the interval and the price approach in writing, and confirm that the client agrees before you change their schedule. Housecall Pro, a vendor, recommends a short follow-up after each completed job about the maintenance plan (8 June 2026). If the written offer goes by email or text, check the electronic message rules first. ACMA's guidance says inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase.

instruction.heading: Check in at the interval that suits the service
instruction.body: For a pool, the check-in can follow the next seasonal visit rather than a fixed number of days. The check asks whether the water still holds, whether anything has changed, such as a new heater, a cracked tile or a cover that is no longer used, and whether there is other work to quote. Keep it short, record what the client said, and close the loop with a reply. A check-in that only asks about the result may not be commercial, but a message that promotes any service can be, even when it is framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 9 November 2023). ACMA's guidance requires an unsubscribe option on every commercial message.

instruction.heading: Re-contact previous clients before their busy periods
instruction.body: Pool work follows the calendar. A pool needs opening before the warm months, a check before a holiday rental season, and a barrier review on the owner's inspection cycle. Plan a short message a few weeks before each period, and offer slots you can actually deliver, with a clear way to opt out. Do not use the message to pressure anyone, and do not contact a client who has asked not to hear from you. ACMA says an unsubscribe must be honoured within five working days, so record each opt-out as soon as you receive it. Barrier work has its own timing that depends on the state. Victoria requires a barrier compliance certificate every four years (Victorian Building Authority, undated), and Western Australian local governments inspect private barriers at least every four years (WA Government, 7 May 2025). In Victoria the owner must use a registered inspector, building inspector or building surveyor (Building and Plumbing Commission, 30 June 2026), so your technician does not sign the certificate. In Western Australia the local government does the inspection. If a client needs a certificate, refer them to the person the rules name for that state, then quote any repairs they list.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: A referral reward works best when the client knows the terms before they refer someone. Decide what you will offer, such as a credit on the next service or a small thank-you, and write down the condition for payment, which is normally that the referred person has completed a paid service. Research on referral programmes found that stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals in the studies reported (Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research, 2023). Get the referred neighbour's consent before any referral message is sent, because the referrer's word alone may not be enough (Clayton Utz, 11 May 2017). Check any cash-based reward, and its tax or contract effect, with an adviser before you start. No business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found, so those points remain unconfirmed.

procedure: After each service is signed off, make one review or referral request and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-service offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and confirm it with the client.
Schedule the check-in for the next seasonal visit, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Plan a re-contact message for each busy period in the calendar, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books, confirm the referred service is paid before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: A pool technician completes a chemistry reset for a regular client on a holiday-letting property. The client says she will recommend him to her neighbour, who has a pool and is due for a barrier check. He wants to offer her a credit on her next visit if the neighbour books.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should he do before the neighbour books, and what should he avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: He writes down the reward terms before any referral happens: the credit, the condition that the neighbour completes a paid service, and when the credit will be applied. He asks his client to pass on the neighbour's details, and he contacts the neighbour only if the neighbour agrees. He does not promise a reward he has not written down. He does not offer to sign or present a barrier certificate. In Victoria the certificate comes from a registered inspector, and in Queensland from a licensed pool safety inspector, so he refers the owner to that person. If he is unsure of the tax or contract effect of the credit, he confirms it with an adviser.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date, the test-log summary and the review or referral request made
Next-service offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of seasonal re-contact dates for opening, spring and holiday seasons
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules and the chemical handling rules of the state where the work is done

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the client has confirmed the water result.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after sign-off, when the client has seen the test log and confirmed the result is right.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a client's name, photo or review without their consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a client who asked not to hear from you, or using a re-contact message to pressure them.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour it at once, and keep re-contact messages factual and optional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a client's name, photo, review or property detail needs the client's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on a client's behalf or invent them. If the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business, client details are also personal information. The OAIC's guidelines (13 May 2026) say the Act covers organisations above a turnover threshold and some others, so check whether it applies to you.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on the review's content. Check each platform's rules before offering any reward.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a service reminder, so check each message before sending.

A McCullough summary dated 3 July 2026 says new unfair trading practice rules take effect on 1 July 2027, including disclosure of auto-renewal and easy online cancellation. If you sell a pool maintenance plan that renews automatically, check the current text before relying on this, and set your renewal terms now.

A referral does not extend the licence or authority of the business that accepts the work. Accept only the work your licence and insurance cover, in the state where the work is done. Pool barrier certificate rules and pool trade licences differ between states, so check the rules for each state you work in. This lesson does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-service offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-service offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the client has confirmed the water result, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next service in writing, with a date, before the client leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a pool client for a review or referral?
options: Before the first visit, so the client feels committed
After the client has confirmed the water result is right
Only when the client has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants to publish a review with their name and a photo of the pool you serviced. What do you need?
options: Their consent for the name and photo you plan to publish
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred person books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to propose the next step for a pool client?
options: At the end of each visit, with a date

sourceReferences: Google Business Profile Help, 'Review links', https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122?hl=en-GB, no date shown. Supports: a business may share a review link or QR code; discounts or goods in exchange for reviews are banned.

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026. Supports: incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on the review's content.

Baylor Keller Center, 'Wait Just a Minute', https://kellercenter.hankamer.baylor.edu/news/story/2024/wait-just-minute-when-ask-online-reviews, 1 June 2024 (metadata says 13 May 2024). One experiment only. Supports: a later reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one.

AMA, 'Asking for customer reviews at the right time', https://www.ama.org/2023/01/10/asking-for-customer-reviews-at-the-right-time-sooner-is-not-always-better/, 10 January 2023. Supports: timing should match the product type.
Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; the Google position it describes was not checked against Google's policy.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Supports: stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals. No figures used.

Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017 (older than 2022). Supports: the referred person's consent before a referral message.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023. Supports: a reminder that promotes any service can be commercial.

ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown; read 2026-11-04. Supports: consent for marketing messages; unsubscribe honoured within five working days; inferred consent is narrow.

Housecall Pro, 'Recurring service agreements', https://www.housecallpro.com/resources/recurring-service-agreements/, 8 June 2026 (updated 9 June 2026). Vendor source. Supports: a short follow-up after each completed job about the maintenance plan.

McCullough, 'Unfair trading practices laws Australia 2027', https://mccullough.com.au/2026/07/03/unfair-trading-practices-laws-australia-2027/, 3 July 2026. Law-firm commentary. Supports: auto-renewal disclosure and easy online cancellation, with the rules taking effect on 1 July 2027 as described.

Victorian Building Authority, 'Pool and spa inspections and compliance', https://vba.vic.gov.au/consumers/swimming-pools/inspections-and-compliance, undated. Victoria. Supports: a barrier compliance certificate is required every four years.

QBCC, 'Pool safety inspector', https://www.qbcc.qld.gov.au/home-building-owners/pool-safety/find-pool-safety-inspector-search-property-psi-login, dated 31 August 2021. Queensland. Supports: pool safety inspectors are licensed by the QBCC, issue certificates or non-conformity notices, and may do minor repairs. Check the current scope.

Building and Plumbing Commission, 'Swimming pools and spas', https://www.bpc.vic.gov.au/home-owners/home-renovation-and-building-essentials/swimming-pools-and-spas, last updated 30 June 2026. Victoria. Supports: the four-year inspection; owners must use a registered inspector, building inspector or building surveyor.

WA Government, 'Councils keep heads above water on pool barrier inspections', https://www.wa.gov.au/government/announcements/councils-keep-heads-above-water-pool-barrier-inspections, first published 9 December 2021, last updated 7 May 2025. Western Australia. Supports: local governments inspect private pool barriers at least every four years.

Gap: no business.gov.au or ACCC guidance on referral rewards was found; their tax and contract effect is unconfirmed. Pool referral volumes and maintenance-plan retention figures were not found in an independent source.

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam (ACMA)
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages cannot be sent without the recipient's permission or consent; messages must accurately identify the sender and include correct contact details; every commercial message must contain an unsubscribe option. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Publisher: ACMA.
